reference: PRD-3.B | PRD-3.B.5-7 Quality-Control Audits Audit 1 — CED Alignment and Scope All 100 questions are confined to Topic 4.2 Monopoly. The CED states that monopoly exists because of barriers to entry (PRD-3.B.5), monopoly quantity is set where MR=MC and monopoly price is greater than MC (PRD-3.B.6), and a natural monopoly has long-run economies of scale throughout the effective demand for its product (PRD-3.B.7). The bank also assesses the Topic 4.2 learning-objective requirements to explain and calculate monopoly equilibrium, firm decision making, consumer surplus, producer surplus, economic profit/loss, and deadweight loss from graphs or tables. Graph integration is substantial: monopoly D/MR/MC/ATC graphs, profit and loss graphs, deadweight-loss/efficient- output graphs, natural-monopoly graphs, and entry-barrier visuals appear throughout. Future Topic 4.3 price discrimination is excluded. Later government-regulation rules for monopoly/natural monopoly are also excluded. Audit 2 — Construction, Difficulty, and Answer Integrity Question count: 100. Difficulty distribution: 33 Easy, 40 Medium, 27 Hard. Each item has five answer choices and one keyed answer. Correct-answer positions are balanced exactly: A=20, B=20, C=20, D=20, E=20. Numerical items were recomputed using MR=ΔTR, Qm where MR=MC, Pm from demand at Qm, profit=(P−ATC)Q or TR−TC, producer surplus=TR−TVC, and deadweight loss as forgone surplus between Qm and the efficient D=MC quantity. Two initially drafted hard-item calculations were explicitly corrected before finalization, then the bank was rendered and inspected.
